title: Ezekiel Saw the Wheel
description: The spiritual as Hampton Institute sang it, for 2 to 4 singers: everyone sings the quick, bouncing refrain in harmony, then in each verse the soprano sings a line alone and everyone answers "'Way in de middle ob de air". The refrain, two verses, and the refrain after each.

credits.words: traditional spiritual, as sung at Hampton Institute (printed 1909)

licence.words: public domain: traditional, printed 1909 by Hampton Institute and again in 1927 in R. Nathaniel Dett's edition (Dett died 1943)
licence.tune: public domain: traditional, printed 1909 and 1927 (as above)
licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella; the printed four-part setting (1909, "arranged by the musical directors", and Dett's 1927 edition) was used only to check the chords. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): the tune's own rhythm as Dett prints it, its quick pairs and runs of semiquavers, which all four parts sing together word for word, at 84 (Dett marks 90): "in de mid-dle ob de air" in every refrain and verse, "E-ze-kiel", "An' de lit-tle wheel", "An' de big wheel", "by de grace", "'Tis a wheel", and the verses' "go to church fo' to sing", "dey are", "tell you what a hy-po-crit'll" and "an' he'll"; so the lines "'Way in de mid-dle ob de air;" (up to 4.1 syllables a second), "An' de lit-tle wheel run by faith," and each verse's first line run faster than three syllables a second. They are the song's own words and rhythm; slowing further would drag.
licence.source: tune and words from R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (Hampton Institute Press, Hampton, Va., 1927), pp. 60 to 61, "Ezekiel Saw de Wheel" (Robert Nathaniel Dett, 1882 to 1943), the same setting as Religious Folk Songs of the Negro as Sung on the Plantations, New Edition, "arranged by the musical directors" of the Hampton Normal and Agricultural Institute (The Institute Press, Hampton, Va., 1909), pp. 164 to 165; in A-flat in 2/4, crotchet = 90, and written here a semitone down in G at 84; the refrain, then verses 1 and 2 of the three printed ("Some go to church fo' to sing an' shout" and "Let me tell you what a hypocrit'll do"), each followed by the refrain (D.C.); the answer's fermata is held 2.75 beats; breaths written in for beginners; read from the scan at archive.org/details/religiousfolkson00dett (leaves n91 and n92)
